title: 金铜仙人辞汉歌
titlePy: Jīn Tóng Xiānrén Cí Hàn Gē
titleEn: Song of the Bronze Immortal Leaving Han
author: 李贺
intro: A bronze statue is hauled away from a fallen dynasty’s palace — and weeps. Li He’s strange, sorrowful poem contains one of the most quoted lines in Chinese: “If heaven had feelings, heaven too would grow old.”
analysis: 汉武帝曾在长安建了一座铜人，手捧铜盘承接露水，想喝了长生不老。几百年后，魏明帝下令把铜人拆下运往洛阳，传说铜人被搬上车时流下了眼泪。李贺就写了这个故事。开头说：葬在茂陵的汉武帝，像秋风里匆匆来去的过客，夜里还能听见他的马叫，天亮却毫无踪影。宫殿里桂树还在飘香，三十六宫却长满了青苔。接着写魏国官员拉着铜人上路，东关的冷风刺痛眼睛；铜人只带着汉朝的月亮出了宫门，想起旧主，流下像铅水一样沉重的眼泪。路边枯萎的兰花为它送行，“天若有情天亦老”——老天如果有感情，也会因为悲伤而变老。最后铜人捧着盘子在荒凉的月下独自远去，渭城越来越远，水声越来越小。全诗写朝代兴亡、人生无常，也寄托了李贺自己的感伤。
analysisEn: Emperor Wu of Han once set up a bronze immortal in Chang’an, holding a plate to catch dew; drinking the dew was supposed to make him live forever. Centuries later, after the Han had fallen, Emperor Ming of Wei ordered the statue carried off to Luoyang — and legend says it wept as it was loaded onto the cart. Li He imagines that journey. Emperor Wu, buried in the Maoling tomb, was only a passing guest in the autumn wind: at night his horses can still be heard neighing, at dawn there is no trace. Osmanthus still scents the painted railings, but the thirty-six palaces are green with moss. Wei officials drag the statue eastward; a bitter wind stings its eyes. It leaves the palace gate with nothing but the Han moon, and its tears, remembering its old master, are heavy as molten lead. Withered orchids by the road see it off — and here comes the famous line: if heaven had feelings, heaven too would grow old with grief. The statue goes on alone under a desolate moon, holding its plate, while the city of Weicheng falls behind and the sound of the river fades. The poem is about the rise and fall of dynasties and the fact that nothing lasts — not even an emperor who wanted to live forever. Li He, of royal descent but shut out of an official career, pours his own sadness into the bronze figure.
background: Li He (790–816), a distant member of the Tang royal family, wrote this around 813 after resigning a minor court post because of illness. The story of the weeping bronze statue comes from older historical anecdotes about the year 237.
pronunciation: 多音字：空将 jiāng（带着）；衰兰 shuāi。生僻字：嘶 sī（马叫）、眸 móu、铅 qiān、渭 wèi、携 xié。
version: 采用通行版本，只收正文十二句；原诗有一段小序，讲铜人被拆运的故事，网站不收，内容放在解析里。

lines.py: mào líng liú láng qiū fēng kè
lines.lit: Master Liu of Maoling, a guest in the autumn wind:
lines.en: The Han emperor in his tomb was a passing guest of the autumn wind;

lines.py: yè wén mǎ sī xiǎo wú jì
lines.lit: at night horses are heard neighing; at dawn, no trace.
lines.en: at night his horses neigh, at dawn there is no trace.

lines.py: huà lán guì shù xuán qiū xiāng
lines.lit: By painted railings, osmanthus trees hang autumn fragrance;
lines.en: Osmanthus by the painted rails still hangs its autumn scent,

lines.py: sān shí liù gōng tǔ huā bì
lines.lit: in the thirty-six palaces, moss is green.
lines.en: but moss grows green in all thirty-six palaces.

lines.py: wèi guān qiān chē zhǐ qiān lǐ
lines.lit: Wei officials pull the cart, heading a thousand li away;
lines.en: Wei officials haul the cart toward a city far away;

lines.py: dōng guān suān fēng shè móu zǐ
lines.lit: at the east gate a stinging wind shoots into the eyes.
lines.en: at the east gate a bitter wind stabs at its eyes.

lines.py: kōng jiāng hàn yuè chū gōng mén
lines.lit: With only the Han moon, it goes out of the palace gate;
lines.en: It leaves the palace carrying nothing but the Han moon,

lines.py: yì jūn qīng lèi rú qiān shuǐ
lines.lit: remembering its lord, clear tears like molten lead.
lines.en: and, remembering its lord, weeps tears heavy as molten lead.

lines.py: shuāi lán sòng kè xián yáng dào
lines.lit: Withered orchids see the guest off on the Xianyang road;
lines.en: Withered orchids see it off along the Xianyang road —

lines.py: tiān ruò yǒu qíng tiān yì lǎo
lines.lit: if heaven had feelings, heaven too would grow old.
lines.en: if heaven had feelings, heaven too would grow old.

lines.py: xié pán dú chū yuè huāng liáng
lines.lit: Carrying its plate, it goes out alone; the moon is desolate;
lines.en: Alone, holding its plate, it moves on under a bleak moon;

lines.py: wèi chéng yǐ yuǎn bō shēng xiǎo
lines.lit: Weicheng is already far; the sound of waves is small.
lines.en: Weicheng falls behind, the river’s voice grows faint.

words.en: the bronze immortal (a statue holding a dew plate)
words.note: 汉武帝所造，用来承接“仙露”。

words.en: “Master Liu of Maoling” — Emperor Wu of Han
words.note: 汉武帝姓刘，葬在茂陵；称“刘郎”带有不恭敬的意味。
现代汉语有“嘶叫”“声嘶力竭”。
现代汉语有“拂晓”“春眠不觉晓”。
古代说法，现代汉语说“苔藓”。

words.en: a stinging wind (that makes the eyes smart)
words.note: 李贺独创的说法，“酸”是眼睛发酸。
古义是“带着”，现代汉语不这样用。

words.py: tiān ruò yǒu qíng tiān yì lǎo
words.en: if heaven had feelings, it too would grow old
words.note: 千古名句，后人常常引用。
即秦代咸阳故城，在长安附近。

imagery.name: 秋风
imagery.zh: 汉武帝成了秋风里的过客，写出帝王也逃不过时间。
imagery.en: Even the great emperor is just a passing guest in the autumn wind — no one escapes time.

imagery.name: 月
imagery.zh: 铜人只带走了“汉月”，月亮还是那个月亮，朝代却变了；结尾的月光又写出孤独荒凉。
imagery.en: The statue takes only the “Han moon” with it: the moon is unchanged, the dynasty is gone. At the end the moonlight is bleak and lonely.

imagery.name: 兰
imagery.zh: 枯萎的兰花送别铜人，好像草木也懂得悲伤。
imagery.en: Withered orchids see the statue off, as if even plants could grieve.

imagery.name: 泪
imagery.zh: 铜人流泪，把没有生命的东西写得有情，倾注了诗人的感伤。
imagery.en: A bronze statue that weeps: the lifeless thing is given feelings, carrying the poet’s own sorrow.
